status_detail: Three-pass production review published 40 exact, previously absent SHA-256 indicators from Cisco Talos's September 30 UAT-11587 investigation. The selected set spans 20 malicious HTA/WSF stagers, eight Stage 2 JScript downloaders/decryptors, five TestAssembly.dll downloaders, and seven Antino backdoors. Talos directly described every selected hash, documented a five-stage spear-phishing chain affecting approximately 350 endpoints across eight countries, supplied named ClamAV coverage, and published the IOC corpus under CC0 with explicit blocklist-use guidance. The normal ten-per-family limit was exceeded under the documented major-campaign exception because of the campaign's government and national-security targeting, geographic scale, and multi-stage artifact coverage. Daily-Threat-Intel exposed 78 SHA-256 candidates; the latest ten MalwareBazaar export hashes were also reviewed, producing 86 unique intake candidates after cross-source deduplication. Ten candidates already existed, 23 additional Talos artifacts were held back to constrain one-campaign volume, five were rejected because individual-record access or reuse clarity was insufficient, and eight bare MalwareBazaar hashes were rejected without resolved metadata-rich records. Current primary and discovery sources were reviewed for additional exact hashes; no weaker source was used to increase the count.
